Find the Program that Fits Your Goals
Ph.D. and M.S.
Full-time, research-intensive programs. You work with a faculty advisor, conduct original research, and complete coursework alongside lab work.
Best if: You want to pursue original research, work toward a faculty position, or target advanced roles at national labs and R&D organizations.
Learn more about the Ph.D
Learn more about the M.S.
M.Eng.
Coursework-based programs designed for working professionals. You can complete your degree while staying in your current role.
Best if: You have a bachelor’s degree, are currently working, and want to advance your credentials without leaving your job.
Learn more about the M.Eng.
All Ph.D. and M.S. students are fully funded
Every admitted research student receives a stipend, full tuition, and health insurance. No exceptions.
$33k+ Annual stipend minimum
Learn more about funding
What Does Funding Cover?
33K+ Annual Stipend
Doctoral and Master’s Graduate Research Assistants receive a minimum of $33,000 per year
100% Tuition and Fees Covered
Full payment of tuition and fees for all funded PhD and MS students.
Full Health Insurance
Health insurance is included as part of the Graduate Research Assistantship package.
All Graduate Program Degree Options
Doctorate of Philosophy (Ph.D.) in MSE
Fully Funded – Research
The flagship research program at MSMSE. Work with a faculty mentor on original research in materials science and engineering. Prepares graduates for advanced roles in academia, industry, and government research.
Full funding: stipend, tuition, and health insurance
Interdisciplinary faculty across Boise State colleges
Research partnerships: Micron, INL, PNNL, DOE, Boeing
It’s never too early to start your application! Review the Graduate College website for key dates.
Get more information about the Ph.D. program
Master of Science (M.S.) in MSE
Fully Funded – Research
A research-based master’s degree for students seeking advanced knowledge before entering industry or pursuing doctoral study. Conducted in close collaboration with a faculty research advisor.
Fully funded through Graduate Research Assistantships
Thesis-based original research
Students from physics, chemistry, and mechanical engineering are welcome
Get more information about the M.S. program
Master of Engineering (M.Eng.) in MSE
Working Professionals
A course-based professional master’s degree for working professionals with a bachelor’s degree. No thesis required. Designed to be completed while employed full time.
No thesis or research advisor required
Ideal for engineers and scientists already working in the field
Flexible scheduling for working professionals
Learn more about the M.Eng. program
How to Apply
Application Deadlines
Fall admission: Priority Applications submit by January 15. Final deadline is May 15.
Spring admission: Priority Applications submit by September 15. Final deadline is November 1.
Apply early to be considered for the most funding opportunities.
Review the Graduate College website for more application info.
What You Will Need
Minimum 3.0 GPA (exceptions considered with graduate experience)
Transcripts from all colleges attended
Statement of purpose (2 pages max)
Current CV or resume
3 letters of recommendation
TOEFL or IELTS scores (international applicants only)
NO GRE REQUIRED
The MSE Graduate Program does not consider GRE scores for admissions. International applicants should also review the international application requirements from Boise State.
Visit Boise State International Admissions
Where Will You Do Your Research?
Semiconductor Materials
Thin films, device fabrication, and semiconductor processing in partnership with Micron and Idaho’s growing tech sector.
Nuclear and Extreme Environments
Materials performance under radiation, high temperatures, and corrosion. Collaborative research with Idaho National Laboratory.
Energy and Sustainability
Solar cells, batteries, and clean energy materials. Supported by DOE and national lab partnerships.
Computational Materials
Atomistic simulation, machine learning for materials discovery, and multi-scale modeling workflows.
Nanomaterials and Devices
Atomic-scale materials engineering for next-generation electronics, sensors, and biomedical applications.
Biomaterials
Materials for medical devices, implants, and biologically inspired applications in collaboration with health sciences faculty.
Frequently Asked Questions
My degree is in physics or chemistry, not engineering. Can I still apply?
Yes. MSMSE is an interdisciplinary program and actively welcomes applicants from physics, chemistry, mechanical engineering, and related fields. Your background is a strength, not a barrier. Contact us with questions about your specific background.
I am an international student. Is the program open to me?
Absolutely. MSMSE has a strong international student community. You will need to meet the international application requirements from Boise State Global International, including TOEFL or IELTS scores. Funding is available for international students in the PhD and MS programs on the same terms as domestic students.
How do I find a faculty advisor and secure funding?
Reach out directly to faculty whose research interests align with yours before or alongside submitting your application. Most funding is tied to a faculty advisor with an active grant, so connecting early is the most important step. Browse current open research positions or review the faculty directory to find potential advisors.
What is the difference between the M.S. and the M.Eng.?
The M.S. is a research-based degree for full-time students. You work with a faculty advisor, conduct original research, and write a thesis. It is fully funded. The M.Eng. is a coursework-based professional degree for working professionals. No thesis or research advisor is required, and it is designed to be completed while employed.
Are postdoctoral positions available at MSMSE?
Yes. Postdoctoral openings are posted as they become available. Contact faculty directly or check the current open research positions page for active listings.
Ready to apply or have questions?
Our graduate program team is happy to answer questions about programs, funding, research, and life in Boise.
Email msegrad@boisestate.edu or apply directly through the Graduate College.
